# PROLOGUE

*~Pale shapes moved between the trees, silent as the dead.~*

Cold and tired, looking up at the darkening sky. Will reports finding the wildlings dead, but when they return to the spot the bodies are gone. Waymar refuses to turn back. Pale figures step out of the trees: the Others. Waymar fights alone and is cut down while Will watches from a tree. Then the dead knight gets up again. By a stream they find a dead direwolf, killed by a stag's antler, and her five pups. Theon wants to kill them; Jon points out there is one for each of Ned's trueborn children, and Ned relents. As they leave, Jon hears something and comes back with a sixth pup, a silent white runt with red eyes, for himself. She brings news from a raven: Jon Arryn, the Hand of the King, is dead. In Magister Illyrio's manse in Pentos, Viserys dresses his sister for a feast and warns her not to wake the dragon. Thunder rolled far off in the falling snow.

On the ridge, the old weirwood leaned over the road. At the feast Illyrio presents Daenerys to Khal Drogo. Viserys is sure the match will win him an army to retake the Iron Throne; Dany is terrified. Robert arrives at Winterfell with the queen, her brothers and the royal children. At the welcome feast, Jon is seated with the squires so as not to insult the queen.

He watches his family at the high table, drinks too much, and talks with his uncle Benjen about joining the Night's Watch. Outside, Tyrion Lannister gives him harsh advice: own what you are, and nobody can use it against you. Lysa says Jon Arryn was murdered, and that the Lannisters were behind it. Septa Mordane scolds her and the other girls gossip about Prince Joffrey. Jon is the one person who never makes her feel like she's doing everything wrong. At a window of the broken tower he overhears two people he shouldn't, and sees what they are doing. Jaime Lannister catches him at the sill, and pushes him out.
